## The ghost exchange and the same-process waits (`blocks_per_process`) {#sec-ch13-ghost}

### Summary

A ghost exchange fills each block's ghost cells from its neighbours' interior cells. Between processes the
buffers travel through the process group. Between blocks of the same process they are handed over in memory,
and the blocks have to meet to do it: every block's buffers must be packed before any is copied. This section
describes those meetings. Every one of them goes through a single wait, so a block whose job fails ends the
other blocks' waits instead of leaving them waiting for it, and the first error reaches the caller.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Pack each neighbour slab, move it (process group, or same-process rendezvous and mail), unpack it
into the ghosts, refresh the corners; every same-process wait ends when a block job of the Mesh has failed.

**Data.** In: the blocks' interior cells (conserved variables by default). Out: ghost slabs and corners.
Same-process state: the rendezvous state, mail, x1 anchors and column boards, all keyed by the Mesh.

**Placement.** At the start of every stage (`exchange_ghost_zones`), and at the seam and column exchanges
inside the stage.

**Activation.** Always on with more than one block; the same-process path when `blocks_per_process` > 1.

**Guarantee / limits.** The copies are exact. A failed block job ends every same-process wait of its Mesh; the
caller gets the first error once every job has ended.

**Evidence.** @sec-ch13-ghost-tests.
:::

What a ghost holds, the corner convention and the panel-seam interpolation are @sec-ch03. Here the subject is how
the buffers get there when several blocks share a process, and what happens when one of them fails.

### Derivation

No equation: the exchange copies bytes and the waits are control flow. One property is stated and tested: a
Mesh's same-process waits have exactly one place where a thread blocks, so the failure rule below holds for all
of them. In `src/layout/layout.cpp` at the pin, `g_local_exchange_cv` is waited on once, inside `local_wait`, and
`local_wait` has eight call sites: three in the rendezvous, two at the column board, one at the x1 anchor take,
one at the mail post and one at the mail take.[^ghost-count]

### Numerical method

**The exchange.** `MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones` syncs the hydro's conserved variables and then the
scalars, each as pack (`serialize`), launch, and unpack (`finalize`); `MeshImpl::exchange_ghost_zones` runs that
on every block at once on the Mesh's worker pool. Ghost corners are then refreshed: each installed wall function
is re-applied on the slabs the exchange owns in the other directions, so a corner matches the updated column.

**The same-process meetings.** There are four kinds, each keyed first by the Mesh's id.

- *The rendezvous* (`_prepare_local_exchange`): each block records an arrival event on its stream and counts
  itself in; the last block to arrive orders its stream after every arrival, copies all the blocks' buffers,
  records a completion event, and releases the others, who order their streams after it. A generation counter
  separates one round from the next.
- *Mail* (`post_to_local_block`, `take_from_local_block`): the panel-seam reconcile posts one tensor per
  (sender, receiver, tag); a post waits until the previous message with that key was taken, a take waits until
  it is posted. Both waits are capped at five minutes.
- *The x1 anchor* (`pass_x1_anchor`, `take_x1_anchor`): the block above posts its face for the block below; the
  take waits for it, capped at five minutes.
- *The column board* (`gather_x1`): the blocks of one x1 column post their pieces and wait until all are posted.

**The single wait and the failure rule.** Every one of those waits is `local_wait`. It waits on the one
condition variable until its condition holds or, on a worker thread of a Mesh, until that Mesh's worker pool holds
a failed job's error (`g_local_job_failed`, which reads the pool's stored error under the pool's lock). In the
second case it throws "same-process wait left: a block job failed", so the waiting block's job ends too. The pool
stores the first error, releases its lock and wakes every wait (`wake_local_exchanges`). When every job has
ended it orders the caller's stream after each worker's last work, drops the Mesh's mail, x1 anchors and column
boards (`clear_local_exchange`), which no block will take any more, and rethrows the first error. A run without
an error does none of this. @fig-ch13-wait-abort shows the sequence.

Blocks 0 and 2 wait at a same-process meeting (local_wait); the pool stores block 1's error and wakes them; they leave with 'same-process wait left'; when all three jobs have ended the pool clears the Mesh's mail, anchors and boards and rethrows block 1's error to the caller."
#| fig-alt: "Three horizontal lanes for blocks 0, 1 and 2 and a fourth for the pool; block 1 ends with a red cross, the other two lanes wait and then end; the pool lane shows store, wake, clear and rethrow."

: The code of the exchange and the same-process waits. {#tbl-ch13-ghost-code}

Walk-through, failure path: a block job throws; the pool's worker stores the error if it is the first, then calls
`wake_local_exchanges`; every blocked `local_wait` of that Mesh re-checks and throws; when the last job has ended,
the pool (in `run_block_jobs`, through its `submit`) calls `clear_local_exchange` with the Mesh's id and rethrows.
The five-minute caps of mail and anchor are the only timeouts; a cap that passes raises its own message naming
the blocks involved.

### Limits

**The rendezvous state is never erased.** The rendezvous state map ({{< code src/layout/layout.cpp g_local_exchange_states >}})
gains one entry per Mesh and kind of exchange on first use and keeps it for the life of the process;
`clear_local_exchange` drops mail, anchors and boards but not this map. A later Mesh cannot read a stale entry:
each Mesh takes a new id from a process-wide counter when it is built or reset ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::reset >}}),
ids are never reused, and the id leads the key. A new Mesh built after a failed one, stepped in eager and default
execution, matched a freshly built Mesh bitwise, and 30 entries were left in the map at exit.[^ghost-stale]
**Re-stepping the same Mesh after a failure is not supported.** With its state restored from a copy taken before
the failed stage, the failed Mesh raised "local exchange size mismatch" in 8 of 12 runs and matched a freshly built
Mesh bitwise in the other 4.[^ghost-restep] The cause is a hypothesis, not checked: arrival counts left in the
rendezvous state by the blocks that left the failed round, so that the first block of the next round finds the
count complete and copies before the others have packed. No fix for this is in the code at the pin.

Other limits: the blocks of a process must run concurrently, as the Mesh's worker threads do. Blocks stepped one
by one on one thread wait at the rendezvous or the column board, which have no cap, or fail after five minutes at
a mail or anchor wait; the failure rule above does not apply off a Mesh's worker threads. A peer that is slower by
more than five minutes at a mail or anchor wait fails the same way. Switch combinations are in @sec-ch12-matrix.
